review_reference: Owner decisions in chat by D-Eminence: 2026-10-31, records processing Stage 1 (the healthcare-operations purpose for OCR; only doctor, clinician, nurse and lab may ask; under-18s refused; one request at most 24 hours); 2026-11-03, decision 33(6), "all recommended": "numbers: records processing 0104, scanner 0105, support check 0106, SSO 0107, Akos 0108-0113, owner re-signs each"; 2026-11-03, decision 34(1), "all recommended": "the first access request or Access PIN also covers bringing in paper records for 24 h, said clearly to the patient; under-18s still refused", restated for this build as "the first access request or the Access PIN also covers bringing in paper records for 24 hours, said clearly to the patient; under-18s still refused; the patient can still say no". Unsigned: the owner signs.
evidence: In plain words, applying 0104 to production does this. (1) It switches on the purpose of use "Records processing" (code healthcare-operations), the purpose the OCR service already uses to turn a patient's paper records into their digital record at a facility. Nobody gets access from the migration itself: no grant is seeded. (2) Only staff whose role may run OCR jobs (doctor, clinician, nurse, laboratory) can ask a patient for it; pharmacists and receptionists are refused. A request for a patient under 18, or with no date of birth on record, is refused. A request asks to read or write records for at most 24 hours. The patient sees the purpose on the request in the app and approves or denies it. (3) Owner decision 34(1): when the patient approves a facility's ordinary (direct-care) access request, or gives their Access PIN, that same staff member at that same facility may also bring in the patient's paper records (OCR) for up to 24 hours from the start of that access, and never after the access ends. It does not apply to a patient under 18 or with no date of birth, to another staff member or another facility, to emergency (break-glass) access, to a patient share, or to staff whose role may not run OCR jobs. The patient can still say no: denying the request, ending the access, turning the PIN off or a deny instruction ends it at once; a separate records-processing request still works as before. Staff and services see which access covered each check, and audit records it as today. The website must say this clearly to the patient on the approval and PIN screens before the backend release (the website lane carries those words). (4) The patient's list of access requests gains one column, the purpose; today's Identity reads the old columns by name and keeps working. Nothing else changes: no table, row-level security policy, role or permission; break-glass stays emergency only; the PIN still opens the chart for reading only; publishing into the chart stays a direct-care step. Shipped in the same backend release: Identity names the two refusals (403 RECORDS_PROCESSING_NOT_ALLOWED, 422 RECORDS_PROCESSING_MINOR), returns the purpose on the patient's list and names the covering access; EHR refuses the purpose on imported records and attachments, the reported health profile and OCR's note import, and Lab and Pharmacy refuse it everywhere, so records processing never opens the chart. Kill switch, no release needed: update identity.purpose_of_use_codes set active = false where code = 'healthcare-operations' (new requests refused; every records-processing grant and every cover stop until it is on again). While it applies, new access requests wait a few milliseconds; reads are not blocked; if it cannot take its locks within 5 seconds it stops and changes nothing. There is no down migration; rolling the images back leaves 0104 in place and the earlier images work with it (an earlier Identity answers a covered check as not allowed, so OCR refuses with 403 until the new Identity serves). Technical record: 0104_records_processing_purpose.sql (ported from local branch rp-be 3926c07a, where it was 0100, onto production 34d69557 with migrations through 0103; rp-be is unchanged) is backward compatible. What changes: (1) ('healthcare-operations', 'Records processing', active, 'hid') in identity.purpose_of_use_codes, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. (2) identity.list_my_access_requests() dropped and recreated with a twelfth, last column purpose_of_use (0072's body otherwise, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, owner kept, EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime only). (3) Trigger access_requests_records_processing BEFORE INSERT ON identity.access_requests WHEN (purpose_of_use = 'healthcare-operations' AND NOT break_glass), function identity.access_requests_records_processing() (plpgsql, SECURITY DEFINER, no EXECUTE for any role): 42501 RECORDS_PROCESSING_NOT_ALLOWED unless auth.membership_has_permission(actor, row membership, row facility, 'ocr.job.write'); 22023 RECORDS_PROCESSING_REQUEST_INVALID for another scope or 5-1440 minutes; 42501 RECORDS_PROCESSING_MINOR when dob is null or later than today's Africa/Lagos date minus 18 years. (4) Decision 34(1): identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover(patient uuid, subject text, membership uuid, facility uuid, action text, at_time timestamptz) returns (consent_grant_id, covered_until) or no row (sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, owned by the table owner, EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime only, md5 f3216bee48827dfba8073199b56ded67): an active, not break-glass, not cutover-held, source 'hid', direct-care read_records or write_records grant of that membership, facility, patient and live account, whose request is approved and direct care and either approved by the patient with no authorization method (0072) or both carrying 'patient_access_pin' (0075, 0098); at_time from starts_at and before least(expires_at, starts_at + 24 hours); patient 18 or over on that Africa/Lagos day with a date of birth; the membership holds ocr.job.write; both codes active; no active deny directive naming records processing or direct care (or none) for that facility, organization, staff member or all, 0012's reading. identity.has_active_consent_grant keeps 0012's body, owner, attributes and ACL and gains one last alternative (purpose healthcare-operations and the cover returns a row); its md5 goes from 8b12ce866ee75cce411a2721795ffb92 to 732d11892dd4e27e1ff9093ae3b7de5a (checked in section 5; later migrations pin the new body; order-routes-cannot-complete's suite now pins both). No policy changes: OCR's and EHR's policies call has_active_consent_grant by name. identity-api's PostgresIdentityProvider reads the cover when the gate allows healthcare-operations and no records-processing grant of its own exists, naming the covering grant and covered_until as consentGrantId and expiresAt. runtime-grants.sql gains, in its 0104 block, the revoke from PUBLIC on the trigger function and on the cover and EXECUTE on the cover for hid_identity_runtime. Preconditions (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501 with nothing applied): 0001-0103 applied (0103's organization application gate md5 186eb4ca420749b8bdb324bdc843bc50 and 0102's identity.demo_story_install as markers); not applied yet ('0104: already applied'); the md5 of the bodies relied on, each measured again on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 database migrated 0001-0103 from 34d69557 (0098, 0102 and 0103 replaced none of them): platform.current_actor_subject cf14c2d4a16d44a79ea9dbef9dc79c2b, auth.account_id_for_subject 4678770cf6a210034740f09422fdfbaa, auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6, identity.has_active_membership bb52953ef1cd08527db61230a671859e, identity.create_access_request f88923a49a180c2180fdedb29bf2eccf, identity.approve_access_request af9482ccb8b9d9aa8486035478ac4e94, identity.has_active_consent_grant 8b12ce866ee75cce411a2721795ffb92, identity.list_my_access_requests 966c38f6e349caff2877316eed101ae3, and the list's eleven result columns; the types and NOT NULLs of the 36 columns read; one owner for the tables and functions involved, the applier that owner or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it; that owner's schema, table and EXECUTE privileges never through a superuser's bypass; row-level security not forced on identity.patients, identity.access_requests and identity.consent_grants. Post-checks pin the code row, every new or replaced function's attributes, result, owner and exact ACL, the trigger's exact definition, has_active_consent_grant's new md5 and unchanged ACL. Locks (pg_locks before commit on a 0103 copy): ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.purpose_of_use_codes and its key; SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.access_requests (CREATE TRIGGER); ACCESS SHARE on identity.consent_grants, identity.patients, auth.accounts, the two directive tables and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the cover's body checked at creation); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the dropped list function, SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the three new functions and has_active_consent_grant; catalog read locks and the session's own temporary objects; no other application relation. Proved on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 as pgrun: a fresh install of 0001-0104 by the runner on a new cluster with no runtime role (plan 105 pending, dry run rolled back with no ledger written, 105 applied, the cover owner-only until the role bootstrap, then EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime; bootstrap --verify-only passes; the runner again reports 0 pending and the file run again stops with '0104: already applied'; all 78 database suites pass); an upgrade of a 0103 database bootstrapped with 34d69557's runtime-grants.sql (plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back with 104 migrations and no cover, apply, 0 pending, '0104: already applied'; the non-owner grants go from 1233 to 1234, the one new being the cover's EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime, and the bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql then changes none; --verify-only passes; all 78 database suites pass). The records-processing suite (112 cases) adds section 10 for decision 34(1): covered by the patient's approval grant and by the Access PIN grant (read and write; direct care unchanged, the PIN still read only), not past the grant's end, not at or after 24 hours from its start (a grant made to last three days), ended by the patient's revocation and by turning the PIN off, refused for a 17-year-old and for no date of birth (also with the PIN), at another facility and for the same staff member's membership asked at another facility, for another staff member, for break-glass (emergency stays emergency only), for a pharmacist's approved grant (no ocr.job.write), for a patient share, under a deny directive for records processing or for direct care, with either code switched off; a separate records-processing request still works; only Identity may call the cover, which names the covering grant and its end. Eight mutants of the cover are killed by it (no 24-hour bound, no age rule, any authorization method (a share then covers), no directives, no ocr.job.write, one code enough, past the grant's end, revoked grants); two are equivalent because the rule is enforced twice (the facility match, also bound by has_active_membership and membership_has_permission; break-glass, also excluded by the approval and PIN rule). The runtime verifier services/ehr-api/scripts/verify-records-processing-runtime.mjs (Identity, EHR, Lab, Pharmacy and OCR booted from their own code as their runtime roles, over HTTP) passes this branch on 0104 (now also: a second patient approves the doctor's direct-care read request and OCR creates and reads a job for that patient, consent-status answers read and write with expiresAt the cover's end, another staff member is not covered, Identity's authorization audit row names the covering grant, the patient's revocation ends it; then the patient's Access PIN covers it the same way and turning the PIN off ends it), this branch's services on 0103 (before-0104), and 34d69557's Identity on 0104 (old-identity: the care approval is not honoured, OCR 403 ACCESS_DENIED, everything else as before). jest and tsc pass for identity-api (1876 tests, with the new postgres-identity.provider.spec.ts), ehr-api (555), lab-api (474) and pharmacy-api (209); the migration ledger, its test and the release contract tests (98) pass.
